title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Guiding Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Cross-Enforcement Work
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Guiding Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Cross-Execution Work

Fa Fa [2024] No. 9

The High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Guiding Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Cross-Execution Work are hereby issued for your earnest implementation in light of actual conditions. If any issues are encountered during implementation, please promptly report them to the Supreme People's Court.

June 17, 2024

Supreme People's Court

Guiding Opinions on Cross-Execution Work

To further strengthen the supervision and management of the people's courts' execution work, promote the legal, standardized, and routine operation of cross-execution work, and accelerate the achievement of the goal of effectively resolving difficulties in enforcement, these Opinions are formulated in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law and relevant judicial interpretations, and in light of the actual circumstances of the people's courts' execution work.

I. General Requirements

1. Work Objectives. Adhere to the guidance of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, thoroughly implement Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law, strictly follow the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law and relevant judicial interpretations, focus on the theme of "justice and efficiency" in adjudication work, fully utilize cross-execution methods such as supervision and urging execution, directed execution, upgraded execution, centralized execution, and coordinated execution to resolve enforcement difficulties, deepen the reform of separating adjudication from enforcement, strengthen execution supervision, and enhance unified management, unified command, and unified coordination of execution work. Effectively address entrenched problems such as passive enforcement and selective enforcement, effectively curb evasion and resistance to enforcement, and effectively eliminate illegal interference with and obstruction of enforcement. Substantially improve the quality, efficiency, and effectiveness of enforcement cases, promptly realize the legitimate rights and interests of prevailing parties, and strive to enable the people to feel fairness and justice in every judicial case.

2. Basic Principles. In carrying out cross-execution work, the people's courts shall adhere to the following principles:

-- Principle of Necessity. Article 235 of the Civil Procedure Law establishes the general principle of jurisdiction over enforcement. The people's courts shall generally determine the court with jurisdiction over an enforcement case in accordance with the spirit of that Article. However, where enforcement has not been effectively advanced for a long period due to factors such as improper interference, passive enforcement, or insufficient enforcement resources of the executing court, or where multiple cases are interrelated and centralized handling is more conducive to enforcement, or where the enforcement case is difficult and complex and requires coordination by a higher-level court or cooperation by other courts, cross-execution may be carried out in accordance with the law.

-- Principle of Convenience. The "principle of convenience for both parties" is an important principle regarding territorial jurisdiction in China's civil procedure. In conducting cross-execution, the people's courts shall, with reference to the spirit of the "principle of convenience for both parties," comprehensively consider factors such as the domicile of the parties, the location of principal assets, the caseload of the executing court, and the strength of enforcement personnel. Starting from the convenience for parties to participate in enforcement and for the people's court to carry out enforcement work in a timely and effective manner in accordance with the law, the cross-execution cases and the cross-execution court shall be reasonably determined.

-- Principle of Standardization. Cross-execution is an important means and effective lever for the people's courts to strengthen execution supervision and management, and must be carried out in a standardized and orderly manner strictly in accordance with legal provisions. Effectively utilize the information management functions of the execution command center, combine methods such as process supervision, quality and efficiency review, handling of complaints and petitions, supervision and inspection, and patrols to strengthen supervision over enforcement cases within the jurisdiction. Use the institutional tools of cross-execution to improve the execution supervision and management system, consolidate the supervision and management responsibilities of courts at all levels, standardize enforcement conduct, and enhance the people's sense of gain and satisfaction.

3. Selection of Methods. Specific methods of cross-execution, such as supervision and urging execution, directed execution, upgraded execution, centralized execution, and coordinated execution, form an organic whole for strengthening execution supervision and management and effectively resolving enforcement difficulties. They are interrelated yet distinct, and are not simply parallel or progressive relationships. People's courts at all levels shall deeply understand the inherent nature and logical relationships among the various methods of cross-execution, and in light of the specific circumstances of the executing court and the enforcement case, adapt to local conditions, tailor measures to the case, and apply cross-execution methods with precision.

Where the same enforcement effect can be achieved, methods with lower costs, such as internal cross-execution and supervision and urging execution, shall generally be given priority. Where directly changing the court with jurisdiction over the case may yield better results, directed execution or even upgraded execution may be ordered directly without prior internal cross-execution or supervision and urging execution. For related cases, they may be centralized under a single court for enforcement. For cases where changing the executing court is not necessary but the enforcement strength of different courts within the jurisdiction needs to be integrated for cooperative enforcement, coordinated execution may be used.

II. On Supervision and Urging Execution, Directed Execution, and Upgraded Execution

4. Circumstances for Supervision, Direction, and Upgrade. Supervision and urging execution, directed execution, and upgraded execution are effective means for a higher-level court to supervise and manage enforcement cases of a lower-level court. Where a case has not been executed for more than six months without justifiable reasons and falls under any of the following circumstances, a higher-level court may, in light of the specific circumstances of the case, order the executing court to complete execution within a specified period, or may direct another court within its jurisdiction to execute the case, or directly upgrade the case to itself for execution:

(1) Where there are issues of passive enforcement or delay in enforcement;

(2) Where the case is subject to illegal interference;

(3) Where the case is significant, difficult, or complex;

(4) Other circumstances requiring supervision, direction, or upgrade.

"Passive enforcement or delay in enforcement" mainly includes the following circumstances: where the debtor has property available for enforcement at the time the creditor applies for enforcement, but the executing court fails to complete enforcement on such property within six months from the date of case filing; where, during the enforcement process, discoverable property of the debtor is found, but the executing court fails to complete enforcement on such property within six months from the date of discovery; where, for the enforcement of obligations to perform certain acts as specified in a legal instrument, the executing court fails to take corresponding enforcement measures within six months from the date of case filing.

"Case subject to illegal interference" mainly includes the following circumstances: where organizations or individuals outside the people's court interfere with enforcement outside the litigation process, causing difficulties in case enforcement.

"Cases that are significant, difficult, or complex" mainly include the following circumstances: cases involving national interests or public interests; cases where there is substantial controversy over enforcement actions; novel types of cases with a "first-case" effect; cases with universal significance for guiding the application of law; cases involving sensitive factors such as national security, foreign affairs, ethnic relations, or religion.

5. Decision Procedure. When reviewing cases for supervision and urging execution, directed execution, or upgraded execution, the people's court shall docket the case as a "Zhi Ta Zi" matter. During the review process, the court shall fully hear the opinions of the applying creditor. If the applying creditor applies not to proceed with directed or upgraded execution, such application shall generally be granted. A decision to supervise and urge, direct, or upgrade execution shall be approved by the head of the execution bureau, and a decision letter shall be issued and served to the relevant courts respectively. The original executing court shall notify the relevant parties and provide appropriate explanations. The decision procedures for other cross-execution methods such as centralized execution and coordinated execution shall follow the aforementioned provisions mutatis mutandis.

6. Case Transfer. The relevant courts shall properly handle the handover of cases involving directed or upgraded execution. The original executing court shall, within seven days of receiving the decision on directed or upgraded execution, transfer the case file materials and a description of the enforcement status to the court receiving the directed or upgraded execution. The enforcement case in the original executing court shall be closed by cancellation after the case is docketed in the relevant court. If there are undisposed funds or property before the transfer of the case, the original executing court shall transfer such undisposed funds or property together to the court receiving the directed or upgraded execution.

The court receiving the directed or upgraded execution shall docket the case within seven days of receiving the case file materials and execute it as a first-instance enforcement case. The amount of the claim in the newly docketed enforcement case shall be the amount not actually enforced, and the enforcement period shall be recalculated. For actions already completed by the original executing court in accordance with the law, such as service, sealing, and appraisal, the court receiving the directed or upgraded execution may choose not to repeat them based on the circumstances of the case.

7. Enforcement Measures. The relevant courts shall ensure proper coordination of enforcement measures for cases involving directed or upgraded execution to avoid situations such as the release of seals or guarantees during case transfer. If, before the transfer of the enforcement case, the remaining period of the relevant control measures is less than thirty days, the original executing court shall handle the renewal of such control measures and then transfer the case after completion. Upon receiving the decision on directed or upgraded execution, the original executing court shall cease enforcement. If emergency enforcement measures are truly necessary, approval from the higher-level court must be obtained. After the case is directed or upgraded, the control measures and other enforcement measures already taken by the original executing court shall automatically become measures of the current executing court, with the period calculated continuously, without the need to issue a new ruling. The court receiving the directed or upgraded execution may handle renewal of control measures upon application by the applying creditor or ex officio.

8. Duty of Cooperation. Where, during the handling of the case, the court receiving the directed or upgraded execution requires necessary assistance or cooperation from the original executing court, the original executing court shall provide such assistance or cooperation. If the original executing court refuses to assist or cooperate, the higher-level court shall order it to do so.

9. Review of Objections. After the transfer of enforcement execution authority, the enforcement review authority shall also be transferred. After an enforcement case is directed or upgraded, if a party raises an objection to an enforcement action of the original executing court or a third party raises an objection to the subject matter of enforcement, the court responsible for executing the case at the time the objection is raised shall review and handle the matter.

10. Re-direction. The higher-level court shall strengthen routine supervision of cases subject to supervision and urging execution, directed execution, and upgraded execution, and shall promptly guide the executing court to carry out work in accordance with the law. If the executing court fails to implement the supervision and urging execution opinion within the specified period, or if the court receiving the directed execution fails to complete enforcement within the statutory enforcement period without justifiable reasons, the higher-level court may direct the case to another court within its jurisdiction for execution, or may directly upgrade the case for execution. Directed execution shall generally be limited to two occasions. After two instances of directed execution, if the higher-level court deems it necessary to continue cross-execution, it shall generally proceed with upgraded execution.

11. Termination of Execution. If, after two instances of directed execution, all property investigation measures have been exhausted, no executable property of the debtor is found, or after lawful disposal and distribution of property, no other executable property is found, the court ultimately responsible for enforcement may, upon reporting to and obtaining approval from the court that ordered the directed execution, rule to terminate execution. Before ruling to terminate execution, the opinions of the applying creditor may be heard. Upon termination of execution, the executing court shall lift enforcement measures in accordance with the law. After termination of execution, if the applying creditor discovers that the debtor has property available for execution, it may apply for execution again with the court ultimately responsible for enforcement. Where the centralized execution court, in accordance with Articles 508 and 514 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, has lawfully distributed the debtor's property and finds no other executable property, it may refer to the aforementioned provisions to terminate execution.

III. On Centralized Execution

12. Circumstances for Centralized Execution. Centralized execution is an important means for the people's court to optimize the allocation of enforcement resources, improve the quality and efficiency of enforcing related cases, and equally protect the legitimate rights and interests of the parties in accordance with the law. Where multiple enforcement cases involve the same debtor, different courts have jurisdiction, and centralized execution facilitates the parties' participation in enforcement and the people's court's timely and effective performance of enforcement work in accordance with the law, a higher-level court may decide on centralized execution.

13. Determination of the Centralized Execution Court. Where a higher-level court decides on centralized execution, it shall generally designate the court that first accepted the case or the court at the location of the principal property to be responsible for execution. Under special circumstances, the higher-level court or another court within its jurisdiction may undertake centralized execution.

14. Case Acceptance and Transfer. People's courts at all levels shall properly manage the acceptance and transfer of cases for centralized execution. The transfer procedures shall follow mutatis mutandis the provisions of Articles 6 and 7 of these Opinions. After the decision on centralized execution is made, if a party applies for enforcement to a court other than the centralized execution court, the relevant court shall inform the party to apply to the court responsible for centralized execution. If the party insists on applying, the case shall be docketed and then transferred to the court responsible for centralized execution. If a court believes that a case it is currently executing should not be transferred, it shall report level by level to the court that made the centralized execution decision.

15. Methods of Centralized Execution. Centralized execution cases shall generally be handled by the same case handler or enforcement team. The court responsible for centralized execution may consolidate related cases into a single case for execution, and the original enforcement cases shall be closed by cancellation. Control measures already taken in the original enforcement cases shall remain effective, and the priority interests of the earlier control measures shall be protected in accordance with the law. For related cases that have not been consolidated but are included in centralized execution, the centralized execution court shall generally take control measures simultaneously to avoid differences in the order of satisfaction among parties due to different sequences of taking control measures.

16. Transfer to Bankruptcy and Participation in Distribution. Where the centralized execution court finds that the assets of a debtor that is an enterprise legal person are insufficient to satisfy all debts or it obviously lacks solvency, it may, with the consent of one of the applying creditors or the debtor, promptly transfer the case for bankruptcy review in accordance with the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Transfer of Enforcement Cases to Bankruptcy Review. If the parties do not consent to the transfer for bankruptcy or the people's court at the debtor's domicile does not accept the bankruptcy case, the property may be distributed in accordance with Article 514 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. If it is found that the property of a debtor that is a citizen or other organization is insufficient to satisfy all debts, distribution may be directly carried out in accordance with Article 508 of the same Interpretation.

IV. On Coordinated Execution and Execution Coordination

17. Unified Deployment and Use of Enforcement Forces. A higher-level court shall, based on the circumstances of the enforcement courts and enforcement cases within its jurisdiction, leverage its coordination and overall planning advantages, and uniformly deploy and use enforcement forces to coordinate and cooperate with lower-level courts in carrying out enforcement work.

18. Comprehensive Coordination of Individual Cases. Where a specific enforcement case falls under any of the following circumstances, a higher-level court may decide on coordinated execution and deploy forces from relevant courts to assist the executing court in carrying out enforcement implementation work:

(1) The case has a significant impact and attracts high public attention;

(2) Enforcement is obstructed or resisted by violence, threats, or other means;

(3) The debtor's principal property or habitual residence is located in another jurisdiction;

(4) Other circumstances requiring coordinated execution.

In coordinated execution cases, the executing court is the main body handling the case, and legal documents shall be issued externally in the name of the executing court. Enforcement personnel from other courts participating in the coordinated execution may, by presenting the coordinated execution decision letter and their work credentials, cooperate in carrying out enforcement actions in accordance with the requirements of the higher-level court and the executing court.

19. Determination of the Coordinated Execution Court. The higher-level court shall comprehensively consider factors such as the caseload of courts within its jurisdiction, enforcement forces, and the location of property, and carry out coordinated execution in a balanced manner, giving priority to assisting courts facing greater contradictions between more cases and fewer personnel, or greater pressure in vacating premises. Enforcement forces within the jurisdiction shall be deployed in accordance with the principle of proximity and convenience, minimizing enforcement costs and preventing frequent or long-distance deployment of enforcement forces from affecting the normal handling of cases by courts within the jurisdiction.

20. Coordination of Enforcement Matters in Other Jurisdictions. In accordance with the Measures of the Supreme People's Court for Strictly Regulating the Management of Commissioned Enforcement Matters (Trial), when a people's court needs to investigate property, control specific property, or release control measures in another jurisdiction during case enforcement, it may commission the relevant court in that other jurisdiction to act on its behalf. Higher People's Courts and Intermediate People's Courts shall earnestly fulfill their supervisory duties, and supervise the handling of commissioned matters by courts within their jurisdiction through the Execution Command and Management Platform.

21. Allocation of Personnel and Cases. A higher-level court may, based on the caseload and enforcement force strength of courts within its jurisdiction, reasonably allocate enforcement resources, uniformly deploy enforcement personnel from courts within its jurisdiction to assist courts with prominent contradictions between more cases and fewer personnel, or transfer cases from courts with a higher caseload to courts with a lower caseload.

22. Circumstances for Coordination of Enforcement Disputes. Where two or more people's courts have a dispute in related enforcement cases and fall under any of the following circumstances, they shall resolve it through consultation. If consultation fails, they shall report to a higher-level court for coordination, and if necessary, report up to the common higher-level court for handling:

(1) Disputes between different courts over enforcement jurisdiction, etc.;

(2) Disputes between the court enforcing the priority claim and the court that first sealed or preserved the property regarding the transfer of disposition authority;

(3) Disputes between different courts over commissioned matters;

(4) Other circumstances requiring coordination of enforcement.

A higher-level court coordinating an enforcement dispute between lower-level courts may, if it deems necessary, issue a coordination decision based on the circumstances. The courts concerned must implement the coordination decision made by the higher-level court.

V. On Supervision and Management

23. Ledger Management. People's courts at all levels shall comprehensively coordinate cross-execution work within their jurisdiction, establish ledgers for cross-execution cases, fully grasp the situation of cases, and conduct dynamic management, supervision, and guidance.

24. Case Evaluation. Higher-level courts shall periodically evaluate cross-execution cases, focusing on evaluating cases of the original executing court that have achieved substantial progress after supervision and urging execution or directed execution or upgraded execution.

25. Assessment and Incentives. Where cross-execution has resulted in significant progress in a case, the court accepting the cross-execution and the relevant enforcement personnel shall be encouraged in an appropriate manner in accordance with relevant provisions, and such encouragement shall be reflected in evaluations, performance assessments, etc.

26. Accountability and Disciplinary Action. Where cross-execution reveals that the original executing court or its enforcement personnel have engaged in passive enforcement, delay in enforcement, or violations of law or discipline, a notice of criticism shall be issued, which shall be reflected in evaluations, performance assessments, etc., in accordance with regulations, and relevant responsibilities shall be pursued in accordance with rules, regulations, and laws.

VI. Supplementary Provisions

27. Filing Requirements. Each High People's Court may, in accordance with relevant laws, judicial interpretations, and these Opinions, and in light of the actual circumstances of its enforcement work, formulate implementing rules for cross-execution within its jurisdiction, which shall be submitted to the Supreme People's Court for review and filing.

28. Effective Date. These Opinions shall take effect from the date of issuance. Any previously issued opinions or notices that are inconsistent with these Opinions shall be superseded by these Opinions.

Annex: Cross-Execution Document Templates

Annex

Cross-Execution Document Templates

1. Supervision and Urging Enforcement Order (for use by a higher-level court to supervise and urge a lower-level court to execute)

2. Request for Instructions (for use by a lower-level court to request upgraded execution or directed execution)

3. Enforcement Decision Letter (for use by a higher-level court to decide on upgraded execution or directed execution ex officio or upon request)

4. Reply (for use by a higher-level court to disapprove a request for upgraded execution or directed execution)

5. Request for Instructions (for use by a lower-level court to request centralized execution)

6. Enforcement Decision Letter (for use by a higher-level court to decide on centralized execution ex officio or upon request)

7. Request for Instructions (for use by a lower-level court to request coordinated execution)

8. Enforcement Decision Letter (for use by a higher-level court to decide on coordinated execution ex officio or upon request)

9. Request for Instructions (for use by a lower-level court to request coordination of an enforcement dispute)

10. Enforcement Decision Letter (for use by a higher-level court to coordinate an enforcement dispute upon request)

1. Supervision and Urging Enforcement Order (for use by a higher-level court to supervise and urge a lower-level court to execute)

×××× People's Court

Supervision and Urging Enforcement Order

(××××) ... Zhi Ta ... No. ...

×××× People's Court:

Your court in the case of enforcement of XXX v. XXX ... (state the cause of action and case number), ... (state the circumstances where the case has been pending for a long time without proper reason / where a ruling, decision, or notice should have been made but was not / where a specific enforcement action should have been taken according to law but was not taken / or other circumstances requiring supervision of enforcement). Pursuant to Article 237 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Paragraph 1 of Article 74 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues Concerning the Work of Enforcement by the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), you are hereby ordered to enforce the case in a timely manner according to law from the date of receipt of this Supervision Enforcement Order, and to conclude the enforcement (make a ruling, decision, or notice / take specific enforcement actions according to law, etc.) by [date], and to report the enforcement results to this court in writing.

By order.

[Date]

(Court Seal)

2. Request (for a lower court to request higher-level enforcement or directed enforcement)

Request for Higher-Level Enforcement / Directed Enforcement
Regarding the Case of ... (state the parties and cause of action)

(XXXX) ... Execution ... No.

To: XXXX People's Court

The case of XXX v. XXX ... (state cause of action) was filed for enforcement by our court on [date], with case number (XXXX) ... Execution ... No.

(Basic facts of the case and enforcement actions already taken)

Our court is of the opinion that ... (state the facts and reasons for requesting higher-level enforcement / directed enforcement). Pursuant to Article 237 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, we hereby request that your court take over the enforcement / direct the enforcement of this case.

We request your approval.

Attachments: X copies of case report

[Date]

(Court Seal)

3. Enforcement Decision (for a higher court to, upon request or ex officio, take over enforcement or direct enforcement)

XXXX People's Court

Enforcement Decision

(XXXX) ... Execution Other ... No.

To: XXXX People's Court, XXXX People's Court:

Regarding the case of XXX v. XXX ... (state cause of action and case number), (XXXX People's Court has requested that this court take over enforcement / direct enforcement), because ... (state the reasons for taking over enforcement / directing enforcement), pursuant to Article 237 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Paragraph 2 of Article 74 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues Concerning the Work of Enforcement by the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), it is decided as follows:

The civil judgment (XXXX) ... Civil ... No. (or other effective legal instrument) of XXXX People's Court (or the authority that issued the other effective legal instrument) shall be enforced by this court / by XXXX People's Court.

XXXX People's Court (the original enforcement court) shall transfer all relevant case files to this court / to XXXX People's Court within 7 days from the date of receipt of this decision, and shall notify the relevant parties.

This decision shall be executed immediately.

[Date]

(Court Seal)

4. Reply (for a higher court to disapprove a request for higher-level enforcement or directed enforcement)

Reply Regarding the Request for Higher-Level Enforcement / Directed Enforcement
of the Case of ... (state the parties and cause of action)

(XXXX) ... Execution Other ... No.

To: XXXX People's Court:

Regarding your court's request for higher-level enforcement / directed enforcement of the case of XXX v. XXX ... (state cause of action and case number), this court, upon review, finds that ... (reasons and analysis for disapproving the request for higher-level enforcement / directed enforcement). It is hereby replied as follows:

It is not approved that this court take over the enforcement of ... case / it is not approved that ... case be directed for enforcement. Please promote the enforcement work of the case according to law.

This is a reply.

[Date]

(Court Seal)

5. Request (for a lower court to request centralized enforcement)

Request for Centralized Enforcement
Regarding the Case(s) of ... (state the parties and cause of action) / Multiple Cases

(XXXX) ... Execution ... No.

To: XXXX People's Court:

The case of XXX v. XXX ... (state cause of action) / the multiple cases of XXX v. XXX ... (state cause of action), etc., were filed for enforcement by this court (respectively) on [date], with case numbers (respectively) (XXXX) ... Execution ... No. (if not filed, the time and case number may be omitted; if there are many cases, a separate list may be attached).

(Basic facts of the case(s) and enforcement actions already taken)

Our court is of the opinion that ... (state the facts and reasons for requesting centralized enforcement, including that the same judgment debtor is involved in multiple enforcement cases, different courts have jurisdiction, centralized enforcement facilitates party participation in enforcement and facilitates the people's court in conducting enforcement work in a timely and effective manner according to law, etc.). Pursuant to Article 71 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues Concerning the Work of Enforcement by the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), we hereby request that your court decide on centralized enforcement according to law.

We request your approval.

Attachments: X copies of case report

[Date]

(Court Seal)

6. Enforcement Decision (for a higher court to, upon request or ex officio, decide on centralized enforcement)

XXXX People's Court

Enforcement Decision

(XXXX) ... Execution Other ... No.

To: XXXX People's Court (all courts within the jurisdiction):

XXX, due to disputes with XXX ... (state cause of action), has multiple litigation cases / enforcement cases / other cases that may enter the enforcement procedure within the jurisdiction of this court, (XXXX People's Court has requested this court for centralized enforcement), in order to facilitate party participation in enforcement and to facilitate the people's court in conducting enforcement work in a timely and effective manner according to law, (state the specific reasons for centralized enforcement), pursuant to Article 71 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues Concerning the Work of Enforcement by the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), it is decided as follows:

1. Enforcement cases involving XXX (state the party) (if there are many cases, a list may be attached) shall be centrally enforced by XXXX People's Court;

2. For enforcement cases involving XXX (state the party) that have been filed but not yet concluded, the relevant courts shall transfer the cases to XXXX People's Court for enforcement within 7 days from the date of receipt of this decision;

3. For cases involving XXX (state the party), if a party applies for enforcement, the relevant courts shall inform the party to apply for enforcement to XXXX People's Court.

This decision shall be executed immediately.

[Date]

(Court Seal)

7. Request (for a lower court to request coordinated enforcement)

Request for Coordinated Enforcement
Regarding the Case of ... (state the parties and cause of action)

(XXXX) ... Execution ... No.

To: XXXX People's Court:

The case of XXX v. XXX ... (state cause of action) was filed for enforcement by our court on [date], with case number (XXXX) ... Execution ... No.

(Basic facts of the case and enforcement actions already taken)

Our court is of the opinion that ... (state the facts and reasons for requesting coordinated enforcement). Pursuant to Article 71 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues Concerning the Work of Enforcement by the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), we hereby request that your court require the relevant courts to assist in coordinated enforcement.

We request your approval.

Attachments: X copies of case report

[Date]

(Court Seal)

8. Enforcement Decision (for a higher court to, upon request or ex officio, decide on coordinated enforcement)

XXXX People's Court

Enforcement Decision

(XXXX) ... Execution Other ... No.

To: XXXX People's Court, XXXX People's Court, ...:

Regarding the case of XXX v. XXX ... (state cause of action and case number) being enforced by XXXX People's Court, (XXXX People's Court has requested this court for coordinated enforcement), in order to facilitate the timely and effective conduct of enforcement work according to law, (state the specific reasons for coordinated enforcement), pursuant to Article 71 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues Concerning the Work of Enforcement by the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), it is decided as follows:

In the case of XXX v. XXX ... (state cause of action and case number), XXXX People's Court, ... shall assist XXXX People's Court in carrying out the enforcement work.

This decision shall be executed immediately.

[Date]

(Court Seal)

9. Request (for a lower court to request coordination and resolution of an enforcement dispute)

Request for Coordination and Resolution of an Enforcement Dispute
Regarding the Case of ... (state the parties and cause of action)

(XXXX) ... Execution ... No.

To: XXXX People's Court:

The case of XXX v. XXX ... (state cause of action and case number) being enforced by our court, and the case of XXX v. XXX ... (state cause of action and case number) being enforced by XXXX People's Court, have given rise to an enforcement dispute due to ... After consultation between the two courts, no agreement was reached. Pursuant to Article 67 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues Concerning the Work of Enforcement by the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), we hereby request that your court coordinate and resolve the matter.

I. Basic Information of the Enforcement Cases of the Disputing Parties

...

II. Focus of the Enforcement Dispute and Consultation Status

...

III. Opinions on the Request for Coordination

...

[Date]

(Court Seal)

10. Enforcement Decision (for a higher court to coordinate and resolve an enforcement dispute upon request)

XXXX People's Court

Enforcement Decision

(XXXX) ... Execution Coordination ... No.

To: XXXX People's Court, XXXX People's Court:

The case of XXX v. XXX ... (state cause of action and case number) being enforced by XXXX People's Court, and the case of XXX v. XXX ... (state cause of action and case number) being enforced by XXXX People's Court, have given rise to an enforcement dispute due to ... XXXX People's Court has requested this court for coordination.

This court, upon review, finds that (state the specific reasons for the coordination decision). Pursuant to Article 70 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues Concerning the Work of Enforcement by the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), it is decided as follows: ... (state the result of the coordination).

This decision shall be executed immediately.

[Date]

(Court Seal)
